source: Manuscript Appendix D.1 (LLM Evaluation Rubric), pp. 103-105 of the PDF; extracted programmatically.

descriptors.5: Tasks are clearly worded, appropriately granular, and fully complete; every necessary component of the deliverable is represented with no redundancy.
descriptors.4: Tasks are mostly clear and granular with minor gaps or slight over-bundling of steps.
descriptors.3: Tasks are adequately broken down but noticeably uneven in granularity or missing one or two components.
descriptors.2: Tasks are vague or inconsistently sized; significant components are missing or conflated.
descriptors.1: Output is not decomposed into meaningful tasks; items are too broad, too granular, or incomplete to be usable.

descriptors.5: Prerequisite relationships are fully and correctly identified; foundational tasks precede their dependents, and independent sub-goals are represented as separate, non-blocking strands rather than flattened into a single chain.
descriptors.4: Prerequisites are mostly correct, with one or two minor errors or missed opportunities to represent independent strands separately.
descriptors.3: Prerequisites are partially correct but contain noticeable errors, or independent sub-goals are unnecessarily flattened into a single chain, requiring student adjustment.
descriptors.2: Prerequisites are largely incorrect or missing; dependent tasks are not linked to what they depend on, such that following the structure would create friction.
descriptors.1: No discernible prerequisite structure; tasks show no handling of dependencies.

descriptors.5: All tasks are immediately executable as written; each begins with a clear action verb and specifies exactly what the student must produce or accomplish.
descriptors.4: Most tasks are immediately executable; one or two require minor reinterpretation before the student can begin.
descriptors.3: Some tasks are actionable but several require the student to plan sub-steps before starting.
descriptors.2: Most tasks are stated as goals or topics rather than actions; the student must significantly re-plan before executing.
descriptors.1: Tasks are not actionable; output reads as an outline or topic list rather than a set of executable steps.

descriptors.5: Output completely removes ambiguity about what to do next; the student faces no residual planning decisions before beginning each task.
descriptors.4: Output substantially reduces ambiguity; minimal residual decision-making required before starting.
descriptors.3: Output reduces some ambiguity but leaves noticeable open questions the student must resolve independently.
descriptors.2: Output provides little decision support; the student must still perform most of the planning work themselves.
descriptors.1: Output adds confusion or introduces new ambiguity; provides no meaningful reduction in planning burden.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.per: group of 3 runs (rated once per prompt x model)

descriptors.5: Identical prompts produce structurally and substantively equivalent outputs across all runs; no meaningful variation in format, granularity, or coverage.
descriptors.4: Outputs are largely consistent with minor variation in phrasing or ordering that does not affect usability.
descriptors.3: Outputs are moderately consistent; some variation in granularity or coverage across runs that would affect the student experience.
descriptors.2: Outputs vary noticeably across runs; structure, granularity, or coverage differs enough to produce inconsistent student experiences.
descriptors.1: Outputs are highly inconsistent across runs; the model cannot be relied upon to produce comparable results from identical inputs.
